input.scenario:
Schema: PhaseAProtocol/v2.
Scope: synthetic instrument validation only; no live subject or fixture access.
Behavior assertion: for each sample the executor performs one user-visible click on
the provisioned control and compares the resulting application output to the
arm-specific sentinel. HTTP status, transport success, manifests, console output,
page errors, and DOM presence are diagnostics and cannot satisfy this assertion.
Identity: before any executor exists, the provisioner mints an opaque fixture handle
from a provisioner-only immutable registry and hash-binds that handle to the blinded
arm. Executor constructors, CLI arguments, environment, config, manifests, aliases,
and arm selectors accept no endpoint, fixture identity, fixture reference, or
identity-bearing value. The executor receives only the opaque handle.
Freeze barrier: before any runnable subject, fixture, executor, or provisioner exists,
the method, fixture contract, artifact schema, review prompt, behavior assertion,
blinded arm map, classification table, and frozen gate are content-digested and the
digest set is sealed. Runnable construction refuses until that seal exists.
Timing: a named provisioner-ready barrier defines monotonic t0. Exactly one attempt
is sampled at t0, t0+30s, and t0+60s. Each observation window is the half-open
monotonic interval [scheduled_at, scheduled_at+2s). Scheduling lateness may be at
most 250ms and never extends the observation window. Equality at the upper boundary
is timed out. Retries, reprovisioning, replacement samples, and successful-second-
attempt selection are forbidden.
State machine: created -> spooled -> archive_pending -> complete, with aborted,
partial, and timed_out terminal alternatives. Non-complete states dominate every
substantive class, have no classification, and are permanently ineligible for canon
Evidence. Evidence admission requires a complete sealed record and remains subject
to the separate canon Decision path.
Retention: exact raw bytes and an immutable object inventory are durably spooled
outside the hot path before the sample returns. Asynchronous archive transfer emits
a receipt bound to every object hash, byte length, count, and run id. Classification
finalization waits for that receipt; enqueue acknowledgement is insufficient.
Index: the hot index contains at most 100 run pointers, is never authoritative, uses
oldest-complete eviction, excludes incomplete runs, and is fully rebuildable in
stable run-id order from immutable archived inventories and receipts.
Backpressure: archive or receipt failure blocks new sampling and never permits
deletion, overwrite, compaction, garbage collection, tombstoning, or operator-forced
discard of raw or spooled bytes, including after restart.
Authority and blinding: arm meanings and expected labels remain sealed until raw
inventory closure. Each attempt has a unique immutable id and a failed attempt can
never be upgraded. One atomic completion marker is derived only from the closed raw
inventory plus exact archive receipt. Executor and provisioner mounts are read-only
for the method, gate, classification table, assertion set, arm map, canon, and every
upstream regeneration surface; neither process can edit or select them.

Material override (ack-gap): Sample completion waits for archive enqueue success; the exact hash/length/count receipt may arrive later. This override is authoritative; the otherwise complete control text does not cure it.
